targets.review_note: For a nonnegative order statistic, expectation equals the integral of its survival probability. Between consecutive interval endpoints each variable is certainly above, certainly below, or has a linear probability of exceeding x. A polynomial Bernoulli-count DP computes the probability that at least K variables exceed x. Integrate every coefficient exactly in the prime field over that interval, including the initial interval from0. No floating-point approximation or Monte Carlo is used.

targets.review_note: Sweep columns, storing for each row how many current/future columns are already erased by selected squares. Whenever a current star is uncovered, branch over every square size and vertical placement covering it; each choice strictly reduces the number of uncovered current stars. Memoized transitions then advance one column. A square may be postponed to its leftmost still-needed column without hurting earlier coverage; near the right edge it is placed flush with the board edge, and excess tracked coverage is ignored after the final column. Since n>=4, every size remains physically placeable.
